payload.consequence: No defect reached the published release, and that rests on checks that did run rather than on their absence: 'git diff --quiet 5108579 origin/main' confirmed the trees byte-identical, and the full pre-release check set (fmt, clippy, 138 tests, package file list, publish dry-run) was re-run against the merged tree before cargo publish. Cost was one added verification step and a judgment call at the gate.
payload.expected: Before the first closeout mutation, prove the green-reviewed implementation commit is reachable from the intended published ref, with local branch or upstream status explicitly not accepted as publication proof.
payload.observed: After the user squash-merged PR #6, 'git merge-base --is-ancestor 5108579 origin/main' returned false: the squash produced 750cc61, a new commit carrying an identical tree, so the prescribed commit-reachability proof was unobtainable for a change that was in fact fully published on the default branch.
payload.run_condition: Surfaced at the very end of a long multi-phase run (12 two-axis review passes over a 14-file change, ~26 findings, then branch push, PR, squash merge, crates.io publish and tag); the closeout reachability gate itself caught it, on the first check after the merge.
payload.workaround_taken: Substituted a tree-equality proof between the green-reviewed SHA and the published ref, plus a full re-run of the pre-release check set on the merged tree, in place of the specified commit-reachability proof.
